abstract: Genome-wide DNA methylation patterns in Schistosoma japonicum across host environments and developmental stages have not been systematically characterized. We performed whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) on worms recovered from permissive C57BL/6 mice and non-permissive Sprague-Dawley rats at 24 and 42 days post infection (dpi). S. japonicum exhibited globally low methylation levels (2.10%-2.86%). Hierarchical clustering indicated that sampling time explained the largest methylome differences, followed by sex- and host-associated variation. Worms from permissive hosts showed a more pronounced methylation decrease from 24 to 42 dpi, whereas worms from non-permissive hosts displayed attenuated changes alongside stunted growth. Sex-associated patterns shifted with maturation. Differentially methylated genes were enriched for phosphorylation-related terms and included LMO4, PPIP5K2, SORT1, and KAL1. We identified 242 host/sex hotspot differentially methylated genes (e.g., LYST) enriched for transmembrane ion transport. Together, these results delineate host- and sex-associated signatures and nominate candidates for functional validation.
